newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says tourist resort bomber was Kurd rebel.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says tourist resort bomber was Kurd rebel.

text.p: Turkish officials on Monday accused Kurdish rebels of attempting to strike at a popular tourist resort in planned grenade attacks that went fatally wrong.

Local governor Cemil Serhadli said a woman who died when a grenade she was handling exploded in the resort town of Bodrum was a member of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) known to police in the southeastern town of Gaziantep.
"She left her family in Gaziantep in 1995 to join the PKK," Serhadli told Reuters by telephone. "She had previously been arrested for taking part in pro-PKK activities."
The woman, Kudret Denktas, died in the blast on Saturday night in a public toilet while trying to fabricate makeshift time bombs with five grenades and watches. The other grenades did not explode.
The PKK, fighting for self-rule in the mainly Kurdish southeast of Turkey, has attacked tourist resorts before in an effort to reduce Turkey's valuable income from tourism.
Serhadli said the woman probably planned to set off the grenades at both tourist sites and the homes of members of the security forces.

He said the blast had not caused panic among the tens of thousands of Turkish and foreign tourists in Bodrum, a whitewashed town on the Aegean Sea that is popular with British and German holidaymakers.
"People were out until four o'clock this morning at bars and discos enjoying themselves," he said.
